findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical optimal BST search: retain the best `(distance, value)` pair, return an exact match, and follow only the child on the target's side. The tuple comparison implements the smaller-value tie rule directly, iteration uses constant state, and no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies paid-only LeetCode problem 270 and its Python TreeNode contract. The Reference preserves the nonempty BST, numeric target, smaller-value tie rule, both examples, all three source constraints, and now defines n and h for the branch bounds.

The immutable native source is tied to verified submission 2064293908. Its search initialization, tuple tie comparison, exact-match exit, branch selection, and final return match the app-local source exactly; the only structural difference is the required local TreeNode equivalent versus LeetCode's injected model and wrapper.

The legal balanced 31/127/511-node BST tiers place the target beyond the maximum, forcing the full rightmost search path while preserving logarithmic height. The current source passes at -0.02 relative exponent and 1.00x largest ratio; a correct full-tree traversal passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.62 and 11.13x.

The Approach matches the protected path search and now gives balanced and skewed height bounds, constant-space accounting, the explicit smaller-value tie requirement, exact-match exit, and out-of-range target behavior.

The hash-bound paid-only Reference remains source-fidelity verified with both examples and all three constraints intact. Its one source tree image is now represented by one accessible Mermaid tree with matching nodes and edges, validated by the repository Mermaid gate.
